text.en:
At night Kavi held his hands in front of a lamp and made a bird on the wall. When he moved his hands closer to the lamp the bird grew bigger.
"Shadows change size and sharpness," his father said, "depending on where the object is."

Light travels in straight lines. When an opaque object blocks the light a dark area called a shadow forms behind it. Transparent objects make no shadow, translucent ones a light shadow, and opaque ones a dark shadow.
A shadow is bigger when the object is closer to the light source. A pinhole camera uses straight-line light to form an upside-down image.
When light falls on a smooth shiny surface such as a mirror it bounces back. This is reflection. The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection. A plane mirror forms an image that is the same size, upright and laterally inverted (left and right reversed).
Light travels in straight lines. An opaque object blocks it and makes a shadow.
A shadow grows bigger when the object is nearer the light.
A mirror bounces light back. This is reflection. The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.
A plane mirror gives an upright image with left and right reversed.

problem.en: Why is the shadow of your hand bigger when it is close to a lamp?

text.en: The hand blocks more of the spreading light when it is near the lamp.

why.en: Light spreads out from the source.

text.en: Light travels in straight lines, so the shadow spreads too.
So the shadow is bigger near the lamp and smaller far away.

prompt.en: A friend says a transparent glass makes a dark shadow. How will you correct this?

requiredIdeas.en: A transparent object lets most light through, so it makes almost no shadow.
Only opaque objects make a dark shadow.

points.en: Light travels in straight lines; opaque objects form shadows.
Reflection: angle of incidence equals angle of reflection.
A plane mirror image is upright and laterally inverted.
